title: Planning MCP Roadmap
goal: Expose Odysseus planning as a reliable JSON-first capability so internal agents, Codex and trusted external MCP clients can create, retrieve, update and contextualize roadmaps without losing provenance, gates or operator control.

problem_statement.user_need: Every AI should be able to use the Planning feature to create roadmaps, find existing roadmaps, load the right context and hand back reliable planning state.
problem_statement.current_gap: Planning exists as JSON roadmaps, HTTP routes, Roadmap Lens and planning-source memory capsules, but there is no dedicated Planning MCP tool surface for internal or external clients.
problem_statement.design_principle: Planning truth stays JSON-first. Markdown may be a rendered view only. MCP tools return compact, bounded, source-linked payloads instead of raw planning dumps.

operator_workflow: A plan is developed in the Agent screen or by another AI.
The AI calls Planning MCP to create a validated JSON roadmap draft.
The roadmap is stored in the appropriate project structure and indexed as derived Planning context.
Raptor Memory receives source-linked roadmap summaries, gates and relationships, but not raw private content.
Harbor One receives a sparse structural notification only for creation, deletion, gate blockers or human decisions.
Clicking the notification opens Planning Overview and highlights the changed roadmap or gate.
Agents later retrieve the roadmap and context pack through MCP before executing work.
Routine progress updates are audit logged but do not notify the operator.
workflow_alignment.ui_boundary: The MCP roadmap defines payloads, events and context contracts. Harbor V2 UI behavior is owned by the Harbor Planning Integration Master Roadmap.

current_ui_prototype: Harbor V2 can open a Roadmap Document Viewer from Roadmaps list or Overview graph selection.
The viewer can show a readable roadmap view and a JSON Data mode.
Spark buttons can switch to Agent and pin a roadmap or roadmap-section context bubble.
service_gaps: Roadmap Document Viewer needs a read endpoint that returns one roadmap as readable sections plus canonical JSON.
Editable summary, tasks and JSON need validate/draft/patch endpoints before any write becomes planning truth.
Spark needs a context-pack endpoint scoped to full roadmap, summary, task or gate sections.
Spark handoff needs redacted audit metadata so the user can later see why the Agent received that context.
Notification deep links need stable project_id and roadmap_id references that resolve to the same service payload.

research_evidence.repo_status_observed: dev branch with existing unrelated dirty and untracked work; roadmap is docs-only and must not revert or touch unrelated files.
existing_planning_routes: routes/roadmap_routes.py exposes /api/roadmap/graph, /dashboard, /planning-sources/inventory and planning-source memory status/ingest routes.
routes/roadmap_routes.py already contains visual-agent-programming validation, proposal review, mutation patch, apply and dispatch request endpoints.
existing_runtime_contracts: src/plan_runtime.py validates structured JSON roadmaps where format_decision.source_of_truth is json.
src/roadmap_lens.py projects PlanRuntimeState into a bounded ProgressiveGraphPage.
src/planning_source_inventory.py scans specs/roadmaps and docs/plans for JSON/Markdown planning sources with stable IDs, hashes and bounded previews.
src/planning_source_memory.py builds and optionally ingests planning memory capsules; current JSON roadmaps receive the highest precedence rank.
existing_mcp_contracts: plugins/mcp_server/plugin.py exposes a disabled-by-default policy-gated MCP server over /api/plugins/mcp.
src/mcp_server_tool_policy.py hides high-risk, generic API, private-read, filesystem-read and owner-scoped write tools unless explicit policy options allow them.
mcp_servers/debug_server.py is a reference for bounded stdio MCP tools with redacted outputs and explicit tool contracts.
mcp_servers/vault_server.py is a reference for owner-scoped stdio MCP tools using trusted owner context and rate limits.
official_mcp_reference: The official MCP specification frames servers as providers of Resources, Prompts and Tools over JSON-RPC 2.0.

The specification's security guidance emphasizes user consent, data privacy, tool safety, access controls and clear authorization flows; Planning MCP follows those principles with read-only defaults, dry-run writes and explicit gates.

planning_service_layer.goal: Create one pure service API that HTTP routes, internal MCP servers and external MCP plugins can share.
responsibilities: List and search roadmap JSON sources using the existing planning source inventory.
Read a roadmap by stable source_id or repo-relative path with bounded content and parsed metadata.
Validate new roadmap JSON before any write.
Create new roadmap JSON from a structured proposal or LLM-produced draft, then return a dry-run patch by default.
Build context packs from roadmap, source refs, gates, active node, related files and accepted planning memory capsules.
Normalize public payloads so no absolute private paths, tokens, raw provider outputs or excessive raw content are exposed.

project_storage_and_memory_bridge.goal: Persist validated roadmaps as JSON planning truth and expose derived Planning context to Raptor Memory without raw private content.
responsibilities: Return stable project_id, roadmap_id, gate_id and todo_id values for UI deep links and MCP context packs.
Record source refs, actor, client profile, reason and undo metadata for structural writes.
Treat Raptor Memory as derived, rebuildable planning context rather than the source of truth.
Keep roadmap JSON as the canonical state and Markdown as optional rendered output.

internal_mcp_surface.goal: Let Odysseus agents use Planning through MCP without going through broad app_api or ad hoc file access.
internal_mcp_surface.transport: stdio built-in MCP server managed by the existing MCP manager
internal_mcp_surface.default_policy: read-mostly; write tools require explicit planning_write gate and owner/admin context

external_mcp_surface.goal: Expose a narrow Planning tool group through the existing external MCP plugin for Codex and other trusted clients.
external_mcp_surface.default_policy: disabled by default; read-only Planning tools may be previewed; roadmap creation/apply requires owner-scoped write scope and explicit gate

ui_integration.goal: The V2 Planning UI can call the same service, but UI implementation is not part of this roadmap.
ui_integration.boundary: No frontend changes in this roadmap unless a later UI-owned slice explicitly claims them.

event_and_notification_policy.principle: Planning MCP calls are usually quiet infrastructure. Harbor One notifications are sparse and reserved for structural changes or decisions.

read_only_tools.name: planning_list_roadmaps
read_only_tools.purpose: Return bounded metadata for available roadmap sources from docs/plans and specs/roadmaps.

read_only_tools.name: planning_read_roadmap
read_only_tools.purpose: Read one roadmap by source_id or repo-relative path with parsed JSON metadata and bounded preview.

read_only_tools.name: planning_search_roadmaps
read_only_tools.purpose: Search roadmap titles, IDs, statuses, gates, source refs and bounded previews.

read_only_tools.name: planning_get_context_pack
read_only_tools.purpose: Build a compact context packet for an agent, Codex or UI task from roadmap source, active node, related sources and accepted planning memory.

read_only_tools.name: planning_graph_summary
read_only_tools.purpose: Return a bounded graph summary compatible with Roadmap Lens for one roadmap.

read_only_tools.name: planning_gate_status
read_only_tools.purpose: Return gates, blockers and next safe actions for a roadmap or node.

write_or_mutation_tools.name: planning_create_roadmap_draft
write_or_mutation_tools.purpose: Create a validated JSON roadmap draft from structured input; dry-run is default.

write_or_mutation_tools.name: planning_validate_roadmap
write_or_mutation_tools.purpose: Validate candidate roadmap JSON without writing it.

write_or_mutation_tools.name: planning_propose_patch
write_or_mutation_tools.purpose: Produce an auditable patch proposal for nodes, gates, status or source refs without applying it.

write_or_mutation_tools.name: planning_apply_patch
write_or_mutation_tools.purpose: Apply a previously validated and accepted roadmap patch.

write_or_mutation_tools.name: planning_mark_status
write_or_mutation_tools.purpose: Mark roadmap or node status after validated evidence.

write_or_mutation_tools.name: planning_delete_roadmap
write_or_mutation_tools.purpose: Delete or archive a roadmap through a reversible structural event with undo metadata.

write_or_mutation_tools.name: planning_emit_structural_event
write_or_mutation_tools.purpose: Classify a Planning change as silent or notify-worthy and return the safe Harbor notification payload when needed.

mcp_resources.purpose: Current active planning context for the operator or active project.
Planning MCP safety, scope and write policy.

mcp_prompts.name: odysseus_planning_create_json_roadmap
mcp_prompts.purpose: Guide an AI client to create a JSON-first roadmap draft with gates, slices, source refs and stop rules.

mcp_prompts.name: odysseus_planning_context_handoff
mcp_prompts.purpose: Ask an AI client to load a context pack before implementing a slice.

defaults: MCP Planning tools are hidden from external clients until the MCP server plugin is enabled.
External Planning tools default to read-only.
Roadmap writes default to dry_run and patch proposal, not direct apply.
Only repo-relative allowlisted paths under docs/plans and specs/roadmaps are valid roadmap targets.
No absolute paths, tokens, private raw document content, provider raw output or chat IDs in MCP payloads.
Every write must record source_refs, reason, actor, client profile and audit metadata.
Every generated roadmap must validate before being visible as claimable planning truth.

gates.decision_needed: Approve read-only Planning MCP tools as safe for internal and external MCP clients.
Approve roadmap draft writes to docs/plans or specs/roadmaps for a named owner/client.
Approve applying validated roadmap patches instead of producing dry-run previews only.
Approve reversible roadmap or project deletion with undo metadata and operator-visible notification.
Approve sparse Harbor notification event classification for Planning structural changes.
Approve exact external client, scope, duration, network boundary and audit requirements.

non_goals: No broad generic app_api exposure for planning.
No shell, Python, arbitrary file write or unrestricted filesystem read through Planning MCP.
No UI implementation in this roadmap.
No live external MCP client connection without explicit Go.
No conversion of Markdown into the planning source of truth.
No automatic marking of roadmap work as done without evidence refs.
No visible Harbor notification for every Planning MCP call.
stop_rules: Stop if a tool would expose secrets, tokens, private raw content, raw provider output, raw chat IDs or absolute private paths.
Stop if roadmap creation would write outside docs/plans or specs/roadmaps.
Stop if an external client requests generic API, shell, Python, unmanaged file access or unclassified tools.
Stop if a generated roadmap omits gates, source refs, stop rules or verification.
Stop if existing unrelated dirty or staged files become part of the scope.
Stop if PlanRuntime validation fails and the fix is not a narrow schema/data fix.

slice_queue.objective: Research existing planning, PlanRuntime, Roadmap Lens, planning-source memory and MCP server contracts, then create this JSON roadmap.
slice_queue.done_when: Roadmap exists as valid JSON and cites existing source files.

slice_queue.objective: Implement a pure Planning MCP service contract shared by HTTP routes, stdio MCP and external MCP plugin.
slice_queue.done_when: List, read, search, validate and context-pack functions work with bounded payloads and repo-relative allowlisted paths.

slice_queue.objective: Add an internal built-in stdio MCP server for read-only Planning tools.
slice_queue.done_when: Internal agents can list/read/search/get context packs through MCP without broad file tools.

slice_queue.objective: Expose read-only Planning tools through the external MCP server plugin policy layer.
slice_queue.done_when: planning_list_roadmaps, planning_read_roadmap, planning_search_roadmaps, planning_get_context_pack, planning_graph_summary and planning_gate_status are policy-classified and visible only when MCP is enabled.

slice_queue.objective: Add validated JSON roadmap draft creation and dry-run patch proposals.
slice_queue.done_when: Generated roadmap drafts validate, remain dry-run by default, and include slices, gates, stop rules, source refs and verification.

slice_queue.objective: Build Planning context packs from roadmap metadata, Roadmap Lens summaries, planning-source memory capsules and bounded source previews.
slice_queue.done_when: A context pack contains enough source-linked context for Codex or another agent to work a slice without raw dumps.

slice_queue.objective: Return one roadmap as a bounded Roadmap Document payload for Harbor V2, including readable sections, canonical JSON, gates, tasks and source refs.
slice_queue.done_when: The UI can request one roadmap by project_id and roadmap_id and receive stable data for Overview, Roadmaps list and Document Viewer without frontend-only demo reconstruction.

slice_queue.objective: Support Roadmap Document Viewer edits as validated draft or patch proposals before any apply write.
slice_queue.done_when: Summary, task and Data-mode edits validate against schema, return a diff or draft id, and expose conflicts instead of silently overwriting roadmap JSON.

slice_queue.objective: Build section-scoped context packs for Spark handoff from roadmap document, summary, task or gate.
slice_queue.done_when: Spark returns a bounded context pack with project_id, roadmap_id, section_id, summary, source refs, allowed memory refs and redacted audit metadata.

slice_queue.objective: Record Planning MCP calls with redacted audit metadata and align with existing MCP client profiles.
slice_queue.done_when: Every external Planning MCP call records client profile, tool name, status, gate reason and redacted argument metadata.

slice_queue.objective: Classify Planning MCP events as silent updates or sparse Harbor notifications.
slice_queue.done_when: Roadmap create/delete and gate decision events can produce safe notification payloads, while context reads and routine progress updates remain silent.

slice_queue.objective: Bridge validated roadmap JSON into project storage metadata and derived Planning memory context.
slice_queue.done_when: Roadmap summaries, gates, dependencies and source refs are represented as derived Raptor Memory planning context with stable project and roadmap IDs.

slice_queue.objective: Allow applying validated roadmap patches only after explicit operator approval.
slice_queue.done_when: Confirmed apply writes an allowlisted JSON file, emits audit metadata, validates after write and returns rollback information.

slice_queue.objective: Allow roadmap deletion only as a reversible structural event with undo metadata and sparse Harbor notification.
slice_queue.done_when: Delete returns undo_ref, writes redacted audit metadata, emits one operator-visible notification and can be restored through the planned UI flow.

slice_queue.objective: Run one bounded external MCP client smoke where Codex lists roadmaps, reads one roadmap, gets a context pack and creates a dry-run roadmap draft.
tests: manual external MCP smoke after EXTERNAL-MCP-CLIENT-GO
slice_queue.done_when: Smoke evidence is redacted, no live write happens without PLANNING-APPLY-GO, and Codex can reliably retrieve Planning context.

manual_smoke_requires_go: External Codex MCP client can call read-only Planning tools.
External client cannot write or apply patches without gate.
Audit log contains redacted planning MCP call metadata.

go_language.go: Planning MCP read-only tools exist internally and externally, context packs are bounded and source-linked, roadmap drafts validate, writes are gated and audited.
go_language.partial: Read-only Planning MCP works, but roadmap draft writes or external client smoke remain deferred.
go_language.deferred: External client live smoke, patch apply and status mutation wait for explicit operator Go.
go_language.no_go: Any design exposes generic API, shell, Python, arbitrary file access, private raw content or direct ungated roadmap writes.
go_language.blocked: Planning truth cannot be validated as JSON or the MCP tool surface cannot be classified safely.

recommended_next_step: Implement PMCP-1 service contract first. Do not start with the MCP server itself; the shared service gives HTTP, internal MCP and external MCP one reliable planning core.
